title: Pancreatic cancer: The RAS paradigm shift
abstract:
by Samuel P. Soff, Eileen M. O’Reilly

Treatment approaches for pancreatic adenocarcinoma, an aggressive disease with poor prognosis, are evolving beyond cytotoxic chemotherapy. Recent advances in RAS targeting with small molecules are redefining therapeutic paradigms. Treatment approaches for pancreatic adenocarcinoma, an aggressive disease with poor prognosis, are evolving beyond cytotoxic chemotherapy. In this Perspective, Samuel Soff and Eileen O'Reilly discuss recent breakthroughs and clinical trial results of RAS-targeting small molecule inhibitors, as well as the challenges of treatment resistance.

title: An unexpected function of a cell-cycle enzyme might explain the toxic effects of its inhibitors
abstract:
Nature, Published online: 28 October 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-03288-5

A previously unknown mechanism required for cells to start proliferating has been identified. A combination of mathematical modelling and cell-based experiments shows that the enzyme WEE1 switches off a protein-degradation complex to allow cell proliferation to start, with implications for WEE1 inhibitors currently in trials for cancer treatments.

title: Viral disease outcomes are indistinguishable between experimentally infected bats and rodents
abstract:
by Maxwell J. Farrell, Samantha K. Tucker, Nardus Mollentze, Daniel G. Streicker

A common explanation for bats being a conspicuous source of zoonotic viruses is their purported ability to coexist with viruses without suffering overt disease. Widespread acceptance of the idea that bats have unusual antiviral traits has catalyzed the discovery of unique features of bat immune systems which may have translational value as broad-spectrum antivirals, particularly if they evolved as a byproduct of bats’ unique life history rather than through conventional co-evolutionary processes. Surprisingly, whether bats compared to other host groups suffer less disease from co-evolved viruses or from viruses generally has not been formally assessed. title: Out-of-balance growth enables cost-free synthesis of the flagellum and other proteins in a single bacterium
abstract: The cost of expressing unnecessary genes on growth has been explained at the population level through balanced growth assumptions. However, due to the high degree of stochasticity in growth and gene regulation, it remains unclear how classical growth laws derived from bulk measurements manifest at the level of individual cells. For example, flagellar gene expression, one of the most energy-intensive processes in Escherichia coli, is typically associated with reduced growth rates in bulk measurements. By contrast, we find at the single-cell level that a strikingly opposite behavior coexists: flagellar gene activity is associated with an increase in growth rate. We show that this apparent contradiction, reminiscent of Simpson’s paradox, results from examining in each cell instantaneous growth and gene expression without indiscriminately aggregating the single-cell data like in bulk measurements. title: Challenges and recommendations for implementation of oncology clinical practice guidelines in China
abstract:
by Minzhi Lv, Duanduan Yuan, Yue Suo, Fang Ding, Lijuan Hu, Lei Cao, Yi Wang, Jing Lei, Shenglan Tang, Tianshu Liu

Summary points

As China’s cancer burden continues to rise and treatment becomes increasingly complex, clinical practice guidelines (CPGs) are crucial to standardising cancer care and supporting clinical decision-making. Over the past decades, China has made substantial progress in developing oncology CPGs, transitioning from expert consensus and international adaptation toward domestically led guideline production.This Policy Forum presents an analysis of the optimisation and implementation of oncology CPGs in China. title: Pre-service mathematics teachers’ integration of design thinking in STEM lesson plans: Insights from a qualitative case study
abstract:
by Rüveyda Karaman Dündar

Mathematics is foundational in science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM) education. Mathematics can foster problem-solving, quantitative reasoning, modeling, and creativity across disciplines. This study explores how pre-service mathematics teachers (PMTs) in a Design Thinking (DT)-focused course integrate DT into STEM lesson planning, the factors influencing this integration, and the challenges encountered during lesson planning. 55 senior PMTs at a state university in Türkiye participated in the study. Data were collected through DT-oriented, mathematics-focused STEM lesson plans and an open-ended questionnaire and were analyzed using content analysis. Findings reveal that while many PMTs maintained mathematics as a core component in their plans, the integration of DT was often partial and unbalanced. title: Behavioural and neurogenetic evidence for emotion primitives in the fruit fly Drosophila from an open field test
abstract: Emotions are based on evolutionarily conserved building blocks (‘emotion primitives’) that are present across mammals. Whether these building blocks are found in insects is largely undefined. Here, we employ the open field test (OFT) in Drosophila and focus on wall-following and total walking activity as behavioural indicators of emotion-like states. Wildtype and transgenic flies were subjected to various conditions prior to behavioural testing. The results indicate that wall-following and total walking activity are independent measures that are modulated, with generally increased wall-following observed under aversive stimuli and decreased values under positive conditions, independent of the time of day. The effects of genetic manipulation of selected neuromodulatory systems support their role in modulating emotion-like states in Drosophila. title: Simplifying principles underlying the highly complex peptide motif of the promiscuous chicken MHC class I molecule, BF2*21:01
abstract: In chickens and humans, classical class I molecules of the major histocompatibility complex (MHC) have a spectrum of correlated properties, including cell surface expression and peptide repertoire. Understanding the impact of these promiscuous generalists and fastidious specialists is of considerable interest. The promiscuous BF2 molecule from the chicken B21 haplotype, BF2*21:01, binds a wide range of peptides by remodelling the peptide-binding site, allowing co-variation of the anchor residues at peptide positions P<sub>2</sub> and P<sub>c-2</sub>, and binding of an anchor residue at Pc. title: Knockdown of a regulatory barcode shifts macrophage polarization destination from M1 to M2 and increases pathogen burden upon S. aureus infection
abstract: Macrophages are driven to form distinct functional phenotypes in response to different immunological stimuli, in a process widely referred to as macrophage polarization. Transcriptional regulators that guide macrophage polarization in response to a given trigger remain largely unknown. In this study, we interrogate the programmable landscape in macrophages to find regulatory panels that determine the precise polarization state that a macrophage is driven to. Toward this, we configure an integrative network analysis pipeline that utilizes macrophage transcriptomes in response to 28 distinct stimuli, reconstructs contextualized human gene regulatory networks, and identifies epicenters of perturbations in each case. We find that these contextualized regulatory networks form a spectrum of 13 distinct clusters, with M1 and M2 at the two ends. title: LEM-3/ANKLE1 nuclease prevents the formation of abnormal syncytium to safeguard neuronal differentiation
abstract:
by Siyu Deng, Chaogu Zheng

In animal development, cells exit the cell cycle after a final round of cell division to differentiate into specialized cell types. However, the impact of failed cytokinesis on the fate specification of postmitotic cells, especially neurons, remains poorly understood. We analyzed the Caenorhabditis elegans mutants lacking the midbody-tethered endonuclease LEM-3/ANKLE1, which resolves chromatin bridges during cytokinesis. Using genetic analysis, fluorescence microscopy, and RNA visualization, we found that unresolved DNA bridges lead to the formation of stable intercellular bridges, creating binucleate syncytia between touch receptor neurons and sister cells, which allows thorough cytoplasmic mixing despite independent nuclear transcription. title: Pollinator abundance shapes sexual selection in an angiosperm
abstract:
by Estelle Barbot, Mathilde Dufaÿ, Tim Janicke, Benoit Lapeyre, Denis Orcel, François Rousset, Jeanne Tonnabel

Sexual selection is a central force in evolutionary biology that has been shown to shape phenotypes and population dynamics in animals. While this selective force is increasingly recognized in flowering plants, theory predicts that anisogamy generates sex differences in the fitness benefits of acquiring additional mates—a pattern well supported in animals but with limited tests in plants. Plant studies rely solely on genetic parentage analyses to estimate mate numbers, thereby conflating performance in accessing mates with success in gamete fertilization. Pollinators add an ecological layer, as their behavior and abundance can influence competition for access to mates and their gametes. abstract:

Background

To prevent wildfires, electric utilities may preemptively de-energize power lines (public safety power shutoffs [PSPS]). title: Prognostic value of the systemic inflammation response index (SIRI) in glioma: A meta-analysis
abstract:
by Lixia Guo, Xudong Cao, Lijun Yang, Xiaoyan Zhu, Lan Liu, Huandong Liu

Objective

To systematically evaluate the predictive value of systemic inflammation response index (SIRI) for the prognosis of glioma patients.

Methods

PubMed, Cochrane Library, EMBASE, and Web of Science databases were searched to collect literature on the relationship between SIRI and glioma prognosis from database inception to July 2026. The primary outcome measures were overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS). STATA 15.0 and Review Manager 5.4 software were used, and random-effects models were employed with pooled hazard ratios (HR) and their 95% confidence intervals (CI) to assess the prognostic value of SIRI. Subgroup analyses, sensitivity analyses, and publication bias assessments were performed.

title: Machine learning for predicting mortality in patients with sepsis and its associated complications: A systematic review and meta-analysis
abstract:
by Hanxi Lv, Yan Gao, Aiping Yu

Background

Sepsis remains a leading cause of death in intensive care units worldwide and may be accompanied by complex complications, including encephalopathy, coagulopathy, acute kidney injury, myocardial dysfunction, and delirium, each of which substantially increases the risk of poor outcomes. Machine learning, a promising approach for prognostic prediction, can capture complex nonlinear relationships among clinical risk factors. However, its predictive performance in sepsis and its specific complications remains unclear.

Method

We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library for relevant literature through April 2026. Studies that aimed to develop or validate machine learning models to predict mortality in adult patients with sepsis and its associated complications were included. title: Rethinking neurodegeneration: Placing disease in its physiological context
abstract:
by Joanna Clarke, Sarah Jäkel

Research into neurodegeneration is often confined to a single disease, cell type or mechanism. A new collection of articles explores neurodegeneration within its physiological context, looking beyond diseased neurons to the surrounding tissue microenvironment.
